scope: Only local pinned public upstream source/schema/archive byte review; no original Garmin or guest, no codec/device/phone execution.

static_contracts.claim: Pinned INPUT is channel1; plaintext complete message consists of BE16 0x8001 then InputEventIndication protobuf. Input indications and binding replies are ENCRYPTED|SPECIFIC, control bit clear; BULK encrypted wire flags are 0x0b before fragmentation. Channel-open response uses control bit and id0x0008.

OpenAuto advertises supported_keycodes and optional touchscreen dimensions. On binding request it rejects any unsupported requested scan code; on OK it starts input and replies statusOK (proto2 required field1). It starts input before send-completion, so our stricter completion gate is owner policy, not a faithful existing-send guarantee.

OpenAuto mouse left press/release/move maps to PRESS0/RELEASE1/DRAG2. It sends one TouchLocation with pointer_id0 and no explicit action_index or disp_channel (defaults0). Touch submessage is InputEvent field3; locations field1; action_index2; action3; location x1/y2/id3 are uint32.

ServiceFactory sets videoGeometry800x480/1280x720/1920x1080; mouse coordinates are scaled from local screen width/height into videoGeometry. However TouchConfig advertises local touchscreen geometry, not necessarily video dimensions. No crop/letterbox/rotation/origin/clamp logic is established. Cannot prove that phone interprets advertised dimensions as video or physical pixels.

InputEvent timestamp is uint64; OpenAuto samples high_resolution_clock::now().time_since_epoch() and duration_cast<microseconds> before strand dispatch for key and touch. This is microseconds, not the 8-byte video-media prefix. Its epoch/clock monotonicity, relation to video and current-phone requirements are not established.

Repeated TouchLocation and action_index support encoding more than one location, but neither source implements multi-touch or explains action_index semantics/list ordering/new pointer/released pointer lifetime. PRESS/RELEASE/DRAG alone do not justify Android MotionEvent CANCEL3/POINTER_DOWN5/POINTER_UP6. A schema roundtrip with two pointers is not receiver interoperability proof.

Non-scroll ButtonEvent uses scan_code1 uint32, is_pressed2 bool, meta3 uint32 and long_press4 bool; nested in ButtonEvents repeated field1, InputEvent field4. OpenAuto sets meta0/long_pressfalse; key auto-repeat discarded. Scroll65536 is RelativeInputEvent scan_code1, signed int32 delta2 (-1left/+1right), inside InputEvent field6. Do not encode negative int32 as sint32 ZigZag.

Schema uses proto3 for event and nested touch/button data. PRESS0, pointer_id0, action_index0 and disp_channel0 may be omitted as scalar defaults. The selected touch_event and each repeated touch_location still require message presence, including an empty location submessage for an origin point. BindingResponse is proto2 with required status even OK0.

minimal_safe_own_encoder_policy.evidence_level: Source-backed legacy schema; receiver behavior not tested.
minimal_safe_own_encoder_policy.readiness: Enable only after successful binding response has actually completed transport; this completion rule is own stricter policy.

single_touch.coordinates: Caller supplies values transformed to one explicitly declared geometry. Enforce 0<=x<width, 0<=y<height as own safe policy, not a proven pinned phone boundary contract.
single_touch.time: Explicit uint64 microseconds supplied by owner; monotonic rule/clock chosen and documented by owner.

minimal_safe_own_encoder_policy.multitouch: Bounded repeated locations/unique IDs/action_index can be schema encoded; list index meaning, multi-finger lifecycle and receiver acceptance remain unproven. Do not advertise completed multi-touch or silently invent CANCEL/POINTER_* values.
minimal_safe_own_encoder_policy.buttons: Use only supported/bound scan_codes; is_pressed boolean, meta0/long_pressfalse default. State consistency/release on teardown are own policy.
minimal_safe_own_encoder_policy.cancel: No CANCEL enumerator in this pin. Local gesture-state reset is not an encoded phone CANCEL; any release emulation must be labelled as own behavior.

uncertainties: Pinned repositories are third-party legacy implementations, not official Google protocol specification or current Pixel acceptance.
No source-defined multi-pointer transition, action_index meaning, CANCEL or pointer down/up enum values.
TouchConfig uses local dimensions while events are scaled to video dimensions; phone interpretation unverified.
No established disp_channel semantic; pinned OpenAuto leaves zero.
Microsecond epoch source does not establish monotonicity/phone clock synchronization/video timestamp equivalence.
No real input hardware/rotation/letterbox mapping, phone UI response or performance proof.
